description: NEON IDCT 8x8: port of jidctint-neon.c. 3-tier sparsity (all-zero, sparse rows 4-7, regular). Individual bench: 40ns NEON vs 75ns scalar (1.9x).
Gather-based zigzag reorder: sequential writes (natural order), random reads (NATURAL_ORDER table). Slightly better cache behavior than scatter.
Eliminated zigzag reorder entirely: Huffman decoder now writes to natural order. IDCT just does element-wise dequant multiply. Massive win (-145 us).
NEON-ize dequant multiply: 8x vmulq_s16 replaces 64-iteration scalar loop. Also direct IDCT call on aarch64 (avoids fn pointer blr overhead).
Fused dequant into IDCT pass1 loads: vmul_s16(vld1_s16(coeff), vld1_s16(quant)) during row load. Eliminates intermediate dequantized[] buffer (8 stores + 8 loads saved).
NEON vertical_blend in h2v2: explicit vmlal_u8 + vshrn. No improvement over auto-vectorized scalar — compiler was already generating NEON for the simple loop.

Strided IDCT output: add stride parameter to NEON pass2 so IDCT writes directly into component plane. Eliminates intermediate [u8;64] buffer + 8× copy_from_slice per block (57600 copies/frame). Profile showed 36% of time in decode_image (includes copy overhead). Saved ~45 µs.

DC-only IDCT fast path: when all 63 AC coefficients are zero, skip pass2 entirely and fill 8×8 output with single pixel value via vst1_u8. Detects inside existing sparsity check (left_dc_only + right_all_zero) with zero overhead for non-DC blocks. graphic 640×480: 341→296 (−13%), graphic 1080p: 1772→1422 (−20%). Photo/checker: unchanged.

P4-141 criterion 5 follow-up: sizes other than 8 (and 8x8 IFAST/Float/no-SIMD) now run the safe fixed-size kernels into an exact-size stack block plus a checked row copy inside Decoder::idct_block_into, because the raw-pointer idct_{N}x{N}_strided wrappers already did exactly that (temp block + copy_nonoverlapping), so they were deleted with their 8 unsafe sites. First version zero-filled a 256-byte block for every size and cost +5.7% at 1/8 scale (1x1 blocks); exact-size arrays and a direct 1x1 store fixed it. photo_1920x1080_420, decode_image at 1/8 1/4 3/8 1/2 7/8 1/1 5/4 2/1 (block 1,2,3,4,7,8,10,16), best-of-9, minimum of 3 interleaved HEAD/after rounds: -1.4 +1.7 +1.1 -1.0 -0.7 +0.9 +0.0 +1.2 % (1/1: 13.64 -> 13.76 ms), all within noise.
